Damn, 500GB for $300. That's pretty cheap for top of the line speed. 4x read and 3x write compared to the 850 Pro? Sign me up.

In all seriousness though, is this really necessary? I was under the impression that "normal" SSDs were fast enough. Will having even faster SSDs help performance, or is the bottleneck still in the CPU?

The bottle-neck is always going to be the hard drive. Consider that there are different levels of memory Level 1 and Level 2 cache are on the processor itself. Then you have system memory. Then you have Swap which is on the hard drive.

Accessing Swap is magnitudes slower than accessing System Memory and even that is magnitudes slower than accessing Level 1 cache.

So, having a faster SSD is going to minimize the latency, at least a little bit. It probably won't be noticeable for someone using a word processor, but if you are doing memory intensive work, yeah it's probably worth the upgrade.

Ukraine and Mongolia have agreed to Ukraine constructing, installing and maintaining 150 smaller 10kilowatt wind turbines in the Tok region of the Mongolian steppe. The turbines will be constructed and installed over the next three years. The estimated costs of this project is around $7.5 million USD for Ukrainian-produced turbines and $2.5 million for infrastructure development in Mongolia.

This initial investment over 3 years would be a trial run to determine future long term investments. The factors that would weigh in on continued foreign infrastructure investment would include:

  • Cost decrease of producing wind turbines in Ukraine
  • Revenue from foreign energy production
  • Improved relations with Mongolia

Construction of the wind turbines will occur at the Yuzhmash machine building plant in Dnipropetrovsk, Ukraine.
